clue.text: What it will take to get the President out of the woods?

definitions.text: What it will take to get the President out of the woods?

parts.words: What it will take to get the President out of the woods?
parts.note: read as politics it asks what would rescue a US president named after shrubs from trouble; read literally it asks for the woodland survival skill that leads anyone out of a forest

explanation.surface: Pundits wonder what it would take to rescue an embattled US President from his difficulties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out of the woods' means free of trouble, and the President is George Bush, whose name is also wild scrubland; the answer is the skill of surviving in the wild.
explanation.definitionFit: Wilderness survival skills are exactly what someone lost in a forest needs to find their way out.

clue.text: Slam outside hospital with a narcotic

indicators.note: the word for slam is placed outside, so it wraps around the hospital letter

parts.note: to slam a door is to bang it
H is the standard abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: Someone bangs a door outside a hospital while carrying drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: Indian hemp prepared as a drink or smoked is a cannabis-based narcotic drug.

clue.text: Trim with a design for top hat is, perhaps, not right

indicators.note: the letters are given a new design, a new arrangement, so they are shuffled
the top of a word is its first letter
not tells us to leave out the letter for right from the word perhaps

explanation.surface: A neat outfit includes a top hat, though perhaps it doesn't sit quite right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top' takes H from hat; 'not right' removes R from perhaps, leaving PEHAPS; 'a design for' then rearranges H + IS + PEHAPS.
explanation.definitionFit: Trim as an adjective means neat and tidy, which is the sense of an orderly, seaworthy vessel.

clue.text: Copy out of old books, having university note to add

indicators.note: the copy stands outside, so the old books sit within it

parts.note: to crib is to copy someone else's work
NT, the New Testament, is a set of books of the Bible
TE is a note of the sol-fa scale, also spelt ti

explanation.surface: A student copies passages from old books and adds a note at university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copy out of' looks like copying from the books, but 'out of' means the copy word sits outside them, giving CONTRIB.
explanation.definitionFit: To contribute something is to add your share to a common pool or effort.

clue.text: Smoker's means of identification comes over as being moderately slow

indicators.note: coming over means flipping, so the whole string is read backwards

parts.note: Etna is the smoking volcano in Sicily
DNA profiling identifies people from genetic material

explanation.surface: A smoker's ID card turns up showing they move rather slowly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smoker' suggests a person with a cigarette; it is the volcano ETNA. 'comes over' reverses ETNA + DNA to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Andante is the musical tempo marking for a moderately slow, walking pace.

clue.text: The marine in charge of the heat

parts.note: taken as written
RM stands for Royal Marines

explanation.surface: A marine officer is put in charge of the heat.
explanation.definitionFit: Thermic is an adjective meaning relating to or caused by heat, so it matches 'of the heat'.

clue.text: Dank smell, fish

parts.note: hum is British slang for a bad smell
ID, more often IDE, is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: A damp, smelly place full of fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Dank and muggy both describe air that is unpleasantly moist and damp.

clue.text: Dickensian mound reported

indicators.note: reported means as said aloud, so we want a word that sounds like the synonym

parts.note: a heap is a mound or pile

explanation.surface: A Victorian novelist's description of a pile of earth.
explanation.walkthrough: Uriah Heep is the fawning clerk in Dickens's David Copperfield.
explanation.definitionFit: Uriah is a villain from a Dickens novel, so a Dickensian character fits.

clue.text: Dr Gershwin is a woman

parts.note: MO, a medical officer, is a doctor
Ira Gershwin was the lyricist brother of George

explanation.surface: A doctor named Gershwin turns out to be female.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gershwin' tempts with George, but it is his brother IRA.
explanation.definitionFit: Moira is a female first name, so it is an example of a woman.

clue.text: ''Eureka'' record? Nothing much

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record
O, the figure zero, means nothing
very means much, to a great degree

explanation.surface: Someone shouts eureka over a record that turns out to be not much.
explanation.definitionFit: Archimedes cried eureka at a finding, so the cry stands for an unexpected find.

clue.text: A man comes back a stranger

indicators.note: coming back means the name is read backwards

parts.note: Neil is a man's name

explanation.surface: A man returns home as a stranger.
explanation.definitionFit: An alien is a foreigner or outsider, someone who is a stranger to a place.

clue.text: Study of food in parliament, standards hard to ignore

parts.note: a diet is a legislative assembly, as in Japan

indicators.note: the hard letter is to be ignored, so it drops out of the standards word

parts.note: ethics are moral standards
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: Parliament studies food policy, but members find standards hard to keep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to ignore' removes H from ETHICS, leaving ETICS.
explanation.definitionFit: Dietetics is the science of nutrition and diet, which is the study of food.

clue.text: Little fellow pinching roast cooked for a person of taste

indicators.note: pinching means holding tight, so the little fellow wraps round the other letters

parts.note: a gnome is a little man of folklore

indicators.note: cooked suggests the letters are messed about, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A small chap steals some cooked roast meat for a discerning diner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' gives ASTRO; 'pinching' splits the little fellow after its first letter. A gastronome is the person of taste the surface's thief is feeding.
explanation.definitionFit: A gourmet is someone with refined taste in food, a person of taste at the table.

clue.text: Prince Otto's original ring

parts.note: Prince Hal is Shakespeare's young Henry V

indicators.note: original means the first letter is taken

explanation.surface: Prince Otto has a ring that once belonged to him.
explanation.definitionFit: A halo is a ring of light, such as one round a saint's head or the moon.

clue.text: Proliferates on a basis of untruths — mine going up and up the chimney

indicators.note: in a down clue going up means the word is written backwards, bottom to top

parts.note: lum is a Scottish word for a chimney

indicators.note: a mine word going up in a down clue is reversed

parts.note: a pit is a coal mine
lies are untruths

explanation.surface: Falsehoods spread, while a mine collapses and smoke goes up the chimney.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on a basis of' places LIES at the foot of this down answer; 'going up' reverses PIT to TIP and 'up' reverses LUM to MUL.
explanation.definitionFit: To multiply is to increase greatly in number, which is what proliferating means.

clue.text: Material mostly extorted from writer

parts.note: drab is a dull brown cloth

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter is used

parts.note: bled, as in bled dry, means extorted money from

explanation.surface: Cloth taken by force from an author.
explanation.walkthrough: Margaret Drabble is an English novelist; 'mostly' drops the final D of BLED.
explanation.definitionFit: Margaret is an English novelist, so she is an example of a writer.

clue.text: Saying about 5-0 in face of contradiction

indicators.note: the saying and its contents go inside the face

parts.note: a dial is a clock face, and also slang for a face

indicators.note: the saying goes about the numbers, wrapping round them

parts.note: a saw is an old saying or proverb
5 is V in Roman numerals and 0 looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: A football score of five-nil is described as a contradiction in the face of facts.
explanation.walkthrough: '5-0' reads like a football score but supplies the letters VO; 'about' makes SAVOW, and 'in' sets that between the first two and last two letters of the face.
explanation.definitionFit: A disavowal is a denial, and denying a claim is a form of contradiction.

clue.text: Politician with burst ulcer getting out of crush

indicators.note: the politician is placed with, among, the reworked letters
a burst ulcer is broken up, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: MP, Member of Parliament, is a politician

explanation.surface: A politician with a burst ulcer is trying to escape the crush.
explanation.walkthrough: 'burst' gives CRULE, and 'with' sets the politician in its middle, after CRU.
explanation.definitionFit: To crumple something is to crush it into creases, as with paper.

clue.text: Soon this time, extremely likely

parts.note: the present is this time, now

indicators.note: extremely means the extremes, the first and last letters, of a word

explanation.surface: It will happen soon, this time very likely.
explanation.definitionFit: Presently means shortly or in a little while, so it is a synonym for soon.

clue.text: In wraps, cast around for summer in France

indicators.note: the cast word is placed around the French summer

parts.note: to shed is to cast off, as a snake its skin
ete is French for summer

explanation.surface: Wrapped up, the cast go around France in summer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast' looks like a noun (actors) but is the verb to shed; 'around' splits it after its third letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheeted means covered in sheets, so something sheeted is wrapped up.

clue.text: Some French quietly lubricate strip

parts.note: des is French for some
P, piano, is the musical direction for quietly
to oil is to lubricate

explanation.surface: French workers quietly oil a strip of metal.
explanation.definitionFit: To despoil is to plunder, to strip a place of its valuables.

clue.text: Go off to serve tea without a fry-up

indicators.note: food dished up to serve is laid out anew, so these letters are rearranged
without means the letter a is left out of the word tea

explanation.surface: Food will go bad if the tea is served without a fried breakfast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' removes A from tea, leaving TE; 'to serve' rearranges TE + FRY + UP. A fry-up is a British cooked breakfast.
explanation.definitionFit: To go off is to spoil or rot, which is what decaying food does.

clue.text: Performance cancelled due to lack of a final decision last time

definitions.text: due to lack of a final decision last time

parts.note: a play is a theatrical performance
something that is off has been cancelled

explanation.surface: A show was cancelled because nobody could make up their minds.
explanation.definitionFit: A deciding extra match is staged when the earlier contest ended level, without a winner.

clue.text: Choice of model to enter bay in the Orkneys

indicators.note: the model goes in, entering the bay

parts.note: voe is a word for a small bay or creek in Orkney and Shetland
the Model T was Ford's famous car

explanation.surface: A model chooses to visit a bay in the Orkney Islands.
explanation.definitionFit: A vote is an expression of a choice in an election.

clue.text: Little one sending me up the pole, for example

parts.note: a tot is a small child

indicators.note: sending something up in a down clue means writing it backwards
up completes the instruction to turn the word over in a down answer

explanation.surface: A child is driving me up the pole, for example.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sending ... up' reverses ME to EM. 'Up the pole' means crazy; the pole is a carved totem pole.
explanation.definitionFit: A carved pole is one kind of tribal emblem, so the pole is an example of one.

clue.text: Fish pieces in East Street on the steep side

parts.note: E is the compass abbreviation for east

indicators.note: the fish and pieces are put inside the street abbreviation

parts.note: carp is a freshwater fish
men are pieces in chess or draughts

explanation.surface: Fish shops in East Street sit on a steep hill.
explanation.definitionFit: An escarpment is a long steep slope, the steep side of a ridge.

clue.text: Almost aim for the shield

indicators.note: almost means the last letter is missing

parts.note: a target is an aim

explanation.surface: Almost aiming for the shield.
explanation.definitionFit: A targe is a small round shield, as carried by Highland soldiers.

clue.text: Old tracks, one with old liveliness

parts.note: BR, British Rail, ran Britain's railway tracks before privatisation
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Old railway tracks with one old charm.
explanation.definitionFit: Brio means vigour, verve and liveliness, borrowed from Italian.

clue.text: Game left in court entertains father, first to last

indicators.note: entertains means holds within, so the court word holds the father word
the letter for left goes inside the court word

parts.note: to woo is to court someone

indicators.note: the first letter moves to the end

parts.note: pater is Latin and old public-school slang for father

explanation.surface: A man left in court entertains his father, from first to last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' gives WOLO; 'first to last' gives ATERP, which 'entertains' places after the opening W. 'Court' suggests a law court, but it is the verb to woo.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer names a ball game played by two teams of swimmers.

clue.text: Kind of net put in the ground

definitions.meaning: prefixed to net it makes the worldwide computer network
to bury a body, especially with funeral rites

explanation.definitionFit: Inter means to bury, and as a prefix it makes internet, a kind of net.

clue.text: Hell of a dance

definitions.meaning: in Christian theology, the region on the edge of hell for unbaptised souls
a Caribbean dance under a lowered bar

explanation.definitionFit: Limbo is the borderland of hell and also the dance of bending backwards under a bar.

clue.text: Characteristic habits of poor Lily's feet

indicators.note: poor suggests something in bad shape, so the letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: Lily's feet suffer from her usual way of living.
explanation.definitionFit: A lifestyle is a person's typical way of living, their characteristic habits.
